item.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
item.description: arXiv:2611.33372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations. As an application of this result, we refine the coalgebraic Frobenius to an oriented circle action (i.e. an action of the monoidal category $B\mathbb N$) on the category of bounded-below, $p$-complete $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-coalgebras, confirming another conjecture by the author. The construction is based on Yuan's approach to Frobenius actions via partial algebraic $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Nikolaus

item.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.34174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Brahma, Takeshi Ikeda, Mark Shimozono

item.title: On the Hermitian K-theory of Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2504.03969v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the $\mathbb{G}W$-spectrum (Karoubi--Grothendieck--Witt spectrum) of Grassmannians over divisorial schemes defined over fields of characteristic zero, and, as a corollary, determine their stabilized $\mathbb{L}$-theory spectrum. As part of our computation, we establish split fibration sequences in $\mathbb{K}$-theory, $\mathbb{G}W$-theory and $\mathbb{L}$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Sunny Sood, Chunkai Xu

item.title: Marked Persistent Homology: Circuits and Bordisms
item.description: arXiv:2209.01099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The barcode of a persistence module does not determine the relations among prescribed cycles. We encode these relations by a filtration of kernels in fixed coordinates, whose circuits can ramify into overlapping families and later recombine, unlike the merge-tree structure of degree-zero persistence. The kernels recover the marked image module and admit simultaneous rational bordism realizations. An explicit planar Vietoris-Rips filtration exhibits the circuit changes and their surface fillings.
item.dc:creator: \.Ismail G\"uzel, Atabey Kaygun

item.title: Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II
item.description: arXiv:2308.00903v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we prove several transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields. Given a fixed field $K$ with finite cohomological dimension $\delta$, the two main ones allow to: - construct totally ramified extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta - 1$ when $K$ is a complete discrete valuation field; - construct algebraic extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta-1$ and satisfying a norm condition. We then apply these results to Serre's conjecture II and to some variants for fields of any cohomological dimension that are inspired by conjectures of Kato and Kuzumaki. In particular, we prove that Serre's conjecture II for characteristic $0$ fields implies Serre's conjecture II for positive characteristic fields.
item.dc:creator: Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche
